source_contract_scope: All source branches defined by dispatch/attribute/coercion composition; native dtype/layout equivalence is structural. Upstream coercion/protocol implementation verification remains a dependency, not an exclusion.

dispatch.precedence: The decorator dispatches __array_function__ before the default body. The only relevant argument is a, even for size(axis=...). A non-default implementation's returned value is returned unchanged; if all attempted implementations return NotImplemented, raise TypeError rather than falling back to metadata/coercion.
dispatch.fallback: Exact ndarray/default implementation, or no relevant argument with an override, calls the source Python body. Actual override invocation/body errors propagate. A failure while LOOKING UP the special method is a separate phase: get_array_function clears ANY exception at that lookup boundary and continues with the absent-override outcome. This is phase-dependent, not an error-type/origin whitelist.

lookup.native_exact_fastpath: PyArray_CheckExact(a) returns the cached ndarray.__array_function__ object without special-lookup helper or metaclass lookup.
lookup.basic_skip_rule: These are exact Py_TYPE comparisons, not isinstance checks. A subclass does not qualify for its base's skip. Skips return absent without inspecting a or its type attribute.
lookup.target: For other inputs use PyObject_GetOptionalAttr(Py_TYPE(a), '__array_function__', &res), not instance lookup. Instance-only __array_function__ is ignored. Ordinary lookup on the type object can execute metaclass __getattribute__, descriptors and other Python code; inherited class attributes follow that lookup's descriptor semantics.

outcomes.absent: No method object: default body is eligible.
outcomes.present_None_or_other_noncallable: Present object is collected as an override; no callability precheck converts it to absence. Actual invocation raises TypeError; no attribute/coercion fallback.
outcomes.present_callable: Invoke exactly as specified below, including any binding already performed by type-object attribute lookup.
outcomes.lookup_exception: ANY exception during lookup (including RuntimeError, MemoryError, or an error originating in domain/kernel code called by the lookup) is cleared at this boundary and produces absent override. Its Python error/refcount lifecycle must match the reference. This does not license clearing a later invocation/body/metadata/coercion error.

invocation.general_rule: After successful non-default lookup, call the returned method object with exactly five positional arguments: method(a, public_api, types, args, kwargs). public_api is the dispatched numpy.ndim/shape/size function object; types is a tuple containing the actual argument type(s), not a. Here only a participates, so types=(type(a),). args and kwargs preserve the original public call's positional/keyword partition, and kwargs is always a dict.
invocation.order: General helper deduplicates actual types and orders subclasses before superclasses, otherwise left-to-right; with one relevant argument there is at most one collected type. No axis object is inspected for __array_function__. When there are no non-default overrides, call the default implementation directly; default ndarray method dispatch calls the function's _implementation without repeating that public dispatch.
invocation.return_and_errors: Return an actual invocation result unchanged, preserving object identity and any AD graph. A returned NotImplemented is a deferral; exhausting implementations raises TypeError. A None/noncallable method or a callable that raises produces its invocation error and does not trigger absent-override fallback.
invocation.size_non_None_order: Resolve outer size dispatch first. If its default body runs for non-None axis, call decorated numpy.shape(a) and complete that dispatch/attribute/coercion path before axis normalization, then math.prod. A size override that returns a result prevents all default/nested work.

coercion.rule: Only AttributeError from the attempted direct attribute access triggers asarray(a), with no dtype/order/device/like argument supplied. Any other exception propagates. This includes AttributeError deliberately raised by a property. NumPy's asarray coercion/array-interface/buffer/sequence protocols then determine the materialized ndarray; they can allocate and execute user hooks.
coercion.valid_cases: Python numeric/string/bytes/None scalar objects become rank0 arrays where coercion succeeds; rectangular nested sequences have their discovered shape; existing arrays/buffers use asarray semantics. Ragged sequences without an explicit object dtype are rejected; recursive/cyclic/deeper-than-max-rank structures and failing __array__ hooks follow coercion's errors.
coercion.cost: Built-in getter branch reads metadata only; this does not cover a subtype overriding that metadata. General array-like fallback can inspect/copy all values, allocate, infer dtype, and invoke custom code; no O(rank) or numeric-data-independence guarantee is made for coercion, custom dispatch or arbitrary custom axis protocols.
coercion.dependency: Exact asarray/coercion protocol is an upstream semantic capability. This metadata contract specifies composition and propagation; it is not verification of that upstream implementation.

native_dtype_layout_value_equivalence.domain: An exact ndarray using its built-in getters, or a subtype whose RELEVANT metadata attributes resolve to those same built-in getters. This is not a claim about every ndarray subclass: it may override ndim/shape/size despite inheriting default __array_function__. Actual dimension metadata is authoritative only in the built-in getter branch.

per_operation_guard.ndim: Built-in ndim getter; no overriding dispatch result.
per_operation_guard.shape: Built-in shape getter; no overriding dispatch result.
per_operation_guard.size_axisNone: Built-in size getter; no overriding dispatch result.
per_operation_guard.size_axisNonNone: Default size body, built-in shape getter after nested shape dispatch, and ordinary valid integer/axis container inputs for the stated native complexity. Arbitrary axis protocol code is specified separately and has no metadata-only cost guarantee.

native_dtype_layout_value_equivalence.dtype_classes: All legal ndarray DTypes: bool; signed/unsigned integers of all supported widths; real/complex including reduced/extended precision; endian variants; fixed/variable strings; datetime/timedelta metadata units; void/structured/nested fields; object-reference arrays; subarray/custom DTypes that form a valid ndarray. This equivalence is proved from absence of dtype or element reads in the native getter code, not from executing one representative dtype.
native_dtype_layout_value_equivalence.layout_classes: Within the built-in getter guard: C and Fortran contiguous; transposed/strided; negative/zero strides; overlapping/broadcast views; non-contiguous/aligned/unaligned; readonly or writable; empty/degenerate axes; scalar/rank0; up to reference rank limit. They return metadata for the actual view. These getters require no numeric-buffer copy/scan/kernel/transfer/synchronization; subclass getters, overrides and arbitrary axis/coercion code are not covered by that cost statement.
native_dtype_layout_value_equivalence.structured_subarray_rule: Do not descend into dtype.fields, object elements, or field subarray dimensions. A plain subarray dtype can already have expanded the actual ndarray dimensions during construction; read those actual dimensions exactly.
native_dtype_layout_value_equivalence.values: For fixed actual shape in the applicable count-arithmetic domain, changing numeric values (including NaN, Inf and signed zero), object referents, byte order or physical strides cannot change built-in metadata output. No element needs to be read/executed. This does not prove arbitrary-precision total-size arithmetic for an overflowing dimension product.
native_dtype_layout_value_equivalence.count_arithmetic: Built-in ndim/shape expose rank and individual npy_intp dimensions as Python integers. Built-in size(axisNone) uses PyArray_SIZE→PyArray_MultiplyList with npy_intp multiplication then converts to Python int; when the mathematical product fits npy_intp, it equals that product. The selected-axis default size path uses Python math.prod of built-in shape ints, so it has Python integer arithmetic. Do not equate the two paths for products outside npy_intp without target/build evidence.

ndim.device: No device argument. Built-in getter branch returns host metadata, with no silent accelerator fallback. External providers can handle __array_function__; if they decline/coercion refuses transfer, preserve the resulting error. Delegated outputs may themselves reside on devices and remain unchanged.

gradient.native_metadata: Built-in ndarray getter outputs are Python int/tuple-of-int values, nondifferentiable with respect to element values; do not apply this assertion to an overridden subtype getter and do not fabricate a zero tensor gradient.
gradient.delegated_identity: A custom direct attribute or successful __array_function__ override is returned unchanged. It may be a graph-bearing tensor or container; preserve identity and its existing AD behavior, with no forced detach, scalarization or nondifferentiability annotation.
gradient.selected_axis_custom_shape: For size with non-None axis, a custom shape's indexed factors pass through Python math.prod. Their multiplication may retain/create AD according to their own arithmetic protocol; no blanket nondifferentiability or int conversion is allowed. The native Python-int factors remain nondifferentiable.

AttributeError at metadata attribute access: attempt asarray fallback and propagate coercion/allocation/protocol errors
Initial operator.index(axis) TypeError is caught and iteration of original axis attempted; non-TypeError propagates
Iteration or per-element conversion errors propagate
Index exceeds C-int range: OverflowError
Index outside[-r,r): AxisError
Repeated normalized axes: ValueError
Custom shape not sized/indexable or factors not multiplicative: preserve len/index/math.prod errors
size.operational_semantics: If axis is None, return a.size unchanged; on AttributeError return asarray(a).size. Otherwise call the decorated numpy.shape(a), normalize axis with len(shape) and allow_duplicate=False, then return math.prod(shape[j] for j in normalized_axes). The non-None branch does not consult a.size and may dispatch numpy.shape separately.
size.native_result: For the built-in size getter, Python int converted from npy_intp PyArray_MultiplyList(S); this equals mathematical product(S) when representable. Selected-axis default size with built-in shape factors returns Python int product(S[j] for j in normalize(A)), with arbitrary-precision Python multiplication; empty selection is1. The getter result is neither ndarray nor NumPy integer scalar. Overflow-region native total-count outcome is not invented or silently excluded.
size.native_cost: Total-size native getter O(r) or better metadata work; selected axes materialize shape O(r), normalize k axes and duplicate set O(k) expected, multiply k Python ints. No element scan.

axis.accepted_forms: axis=None is a distinct fast branch. For a non-None axis not already tuple/list, first try axis=[operator.index(axis)]. If that attempt raises TypeError for ANY reason, catch it, leave the original axis object unchanged, and then iterate it. A custom __index__ raising TypeError plus __iter__ yielding[0] therefore succeeds for a non-scalar array. An index attempt raising a different exception propagates before iteration. Tuple/list inputs bypass the first index attempt. Lists, tuples, generators and other iterables are accepted; do not narrow to documented int/tuple forms.
axis.normalization: Materialize the ENTIRE tuple by iterating in source order and applying normalize_axis_index to each yielded element through the CPython-like C-int converter. For rank r, valid j satisfies -r<=j<r and becomes j+r if negative. Only AFTER iteration/conversion finishes, check normalized duplicates with len(set(axis)); if repeated, raise ValueError. Only AFTER that succeeds, index shape factors and multiply. Negative aliases such as(-1,r-1) duplicate each other, but rank2 axis=(0,0,2) raises AxisError on2 before any duplicate check.
axis.side_effect_order: Default size(non-None) obtains shape and calls len(shape) before normalize_axis_tuple. It then attempts initial scalar __index__ if applicable; creates the iterator; obtains/converts each element in order; finishes tuple materialization; performs duplicate detection; finally indexes shape and math.prod multiplies. A later iteration/conversion exception wins over an earlier potential duplicate, and no shape-factor indexing/product occurs in that failure case. Custom __index__/__iter__/__next__ side effects follow this order; no early duplicate short-circuit is equivalent.
axis.type_errors: At the initial scalar operator.index phase only TypeError is swallowed to permit iteration of the original object. Iteration failures and every per-element normalize_axis_index conversion failure propagate; there is no catch around that generator expression. A scalar float fails the initial index attempt then fails iteration, while a float inside a tuple/list reaches the C converter and fails there. Python bool becomes index0/1; frozen NumPy bool has neither nb_index nor iterable behavior, so its single-axis use ultimately fails TypeError after the caught initial index failure.
axis.overflow: Indices outside C-int range raise OverflowError in the converter before ordinary AxisError range checking; no arbitrary modulo or truncation. Out-of-range representable C-int indices raise numpy.exceptions.AxisError (a ValueError and IndexError subtype).

differential_spec: Run each analytical/negative/protocol case against pinned NumPy2.5.4 and Atlas, compare Python types/values/identity where delegated, errors and call order. No differential tests executed here.

benchmarks.native_cases: Compare exact NumPy2.5.4 and Atlas on built-in-getter actual shape metadata for ranks0,1,2,8,64; hold rank fixed while varying element count, itemsize, dtype family and logical strides. Use genuine exact ndarrays/views or subtypes proven not to override relevant metadata, and built-in integer/list/tuple axes. Time arbitrary custom getter/axis/dispatch/coercion costs separately. Preserve synchronization discipline of the actual backend; do not allocate workload arrays inside timed native metadata query.
measurements: per-query latency distribution and Python/binding cost separately
numeric buffer bytes read or transferred (native target0)
total coercion time measured separately for array-like fallbacks
benchmarks.acceptance: Mathematical metadata equality is exact. Reject an element-count-dependent native scan/copy/transfer. Performance budget must be set from counterbalanced same-hardware baselines and analytic O(1)/O(r+k) contracts; no unsupported universal nanosecond target is invented.
benchmarks.hardware: Host CPU plus each Atlas metadata-resident device backend declared in the program. Native NumPy CPU timing cannot qualify accelerator behavior; record device transfer/sync evidence separately.

policy_decisions.boundary: Classify by PHASE, not exception kind or error origin. Any exception arising DURING special-method lookup becomes the absent-override outcome at that boundary. After a successful lookup, invocation/noncallable/body/metadata/coercion exceptions preserve their own source propagation/catch rules.
policy_decisions.internal_typed_context: A typed LookupFailed can record phase/context without introducing a caller-visible error, new fallback, extra lookup/call or changed Python exception lifecycle. It must not prolong exception/traceback ownership or alter cleanup/finalizer behavior versus the reference. An AttributeError absorbed by PyObject_GetOptionalAttr is already an absent result; do not invent a surviving exception.

unresolved_axes.affected_branch: built-in ndarray.size / size(axisNone), dimension-count product outside npy_intp
unresolved_axes.classification: reference-definedness/build-contract question; retained in denominator, no approved exclusion and no automatic reference-bug waiver
unresolved_axes.source_fact: PyArray_MultiplyList uses unchecked signed npy_intp multiplication. Array construction checks byte-size product; zero-itemsize flexible dtype admission prevents deriving count representability from allocation validity alone.
unresolved_axes.required_evidence: Prove all supported constructor/view invariants or characterize exact target/compiler overflow-region reference behavior with authorized runtime/ABI evidence. No arbitrary wrap, saturation, exception or dtype exclusion is asserted.
